rv.q: The Body of Mary is a play that blew my mind. The darkness balanced with humor, the poignant commentary on exploitation, the fascinating venue. All these elements came together to create a true gem.
Beyond their dubious humor, these overextended one-acts intend to comment seriously upon women being forced to submit to misguided patriarchal authority.
What writer-director Katie Cappiello has wrought are three stories on serious matters.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this three-act comedy about different Marys across time—some find it uproarious and gut-punching, while others question its comedic approach to serious women's issues.
